newsitem.title: CHINA: Annan says nations need human rights, democracy.
newsitem.headline: Annan says nations need human rights, democracy.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Saturday that social justice, human rights and democracy were the best defences against many of the problems facing modern society.

Annan, addressing a seminar on the United Nations in Shanghai, said the U.N. had learnt from peacekeeping in different parts of the world that security could not be guaranteed by military action alone.

There must also be economic development and a strengthening of democratic governments, he said. "The best defence against such new global problems as narco trafficking, corruption, and terrorism is a society based on equal opportunity, social justice, human rights and democracy," Annan said.
Many developing countries were impressed with what China had achieved in economic development in the past few years, he added.
"People in the developing countries see in China an encouraging lesson, a nation whose dynamism and industry have brought great progress," he said.

"China's political weight and economic dynamism give her, especially among the developing countries, a unique opportunity to play a distinctive role in the shaping of the post-Cold War political order," he added.

Annan, who began his first visit to China as U.N. secretary-general on Wednesday, said the withdrawal of the state from large parts of the economy was the key to the fast economic growth China has maintained in the past 15 years.

"In today's world, the private sector is a creative source of financial, economic and managerial resources. China and most of all Shanghai have greatly benefited from these aspects of the global economy," he said.
